body: Ok... It seems I was too excited to find a workaround, becouse it doesn't work. If we want to add custom PropertyEditor not in the same place in a property list... For exemple we want to add PropertyEditor of SECOND property in list BEFORE FIRST. Then it'll fetch name and tooltip of FIRST property instead of SECOND :( Added a new scene for it in a minimal reproduction project: [inspector-plugin-bug_2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23190933/inspector-plugin-bug_2.zip)

I'm not sure this is a bug, from the description in the documentation this seems to be expected:
> Called to allow adding controls at the beginning of the property list for `object`.

Compare with
> Called to allow adding property-specific editors to the property list for `object`.

If so this should be documented more clearly, but it doesn't make much sense to me to have a property editor outside of a property

> If so this should be documented more clearly, but it doesn't make much sense to me to have a property editor outside of a property

Actually, it does make sense, since this is the only way for now to overwrite property **order** for inherited classes. I wanted to have specific important property allways on top of all others for a convinient usability.

If it's not a bug, it should be considered as proposal. If we look at [add_property_editor(...)](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinspectorplugin.html#class-editorinspectorplugin-method-add-property-editor) description, nobody would assume that it works only from inside of `_parse_property`. And, of course, we could add a clarification, that it works correctly only inside of it... But it actually works. Technically it works. It fetches property and managed to edit it. In `_parse_category` it even fetch a name of a property.

So I don't see any serious barriers not to implement all other cosmetic stuff to be allways correctly fetched. The property name is not a big deal, it can be solved easily by specifying it manually, but I don't see ways to make the same with documentation comments.

> Actually, it does make sense, since this is the only way for now to overwrite property order for inherited classes. I wanted to have specific important property allways on top of all others for a convinient usability.

That sounds like a hack, I don't think that's expected or intended use from the description in the documentation

If the only problem is the name and tooltip this seems pretty clearly just how it's expected to work, there's no property to fetch data from because there's no property being processed, the context is from the current property, I don't know that it looks anything up at all, which is good for performance

But the fact that it differs for documentation comments might be unrelated to this and some actual bug elsewhere

But given that this usage isn't documented as supported anywhere I don't think it's expected to
